key_idea: The string is self-similar: A_0 = 0^K 1, A_j = (A_{j-1})^K 1, and after A_{K-1} (which ends in K ones) everything is 1.
sketch: Found by brute forcing small K and reading off the structure. Lengths satisfy len_j = K*len_{j-1}+1 and ones_j = K*ones_{j-1}+1, so only about log_K N levels are needed. Count ones in a prefix recursively: full copies of A_{j-1} contribute q*ones_{j-1}, recurse on the remainder; the trailing extra 1 is only counted when the whole block is taken. If N exceeds len_{K-1} add the surplus as ones. Pitfalls: stop building levels at K-1 or once len >= N (avoids overflow), and large K simply gives floor(N/(K+1))-style counts. Verified against an O(N^2 K) brute force for K=2..7.
